chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Khalid Al-'Ammi, from Khazir Bin 'Amro, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying:
The believer is (of) two believers: a believer who is loyal to Allah with His Stipulations which He Stipulated upon him.
so that one would be with the Prophets and the Truthful and the Martyrs and the Righteous, and a goodly company are they! [4:69]
And that would be the one who intercedes and is not interceded for, and that one is from those who are afflicted neither by the horrors of the world nor the horrors of the Hereafter.

And there is a believer whose foot has wavered with him, so that one is like the stalk of the crop — whichever way the wind tilts him he tilts — and that one is from those who are afflicted by the horrors of the world and the Hereafter, and he would be interceded for, and he is upon good.

key_terms.أَهْوَالُ: horrors/terrors — the fearful calamities and distresses of this world and the Hereafter
key_terms.الشُّهَدَاءِ: the Martyrs — those who give their lives in the path of Allah and attain the highest rank
key_terms.الصِّدِّيقِينَ: the Truthful ones — those of supreme and absolute sincerity and truthfulness in faith and deed
key_terms.خَامَةِ الزَّرْعِ: stalk of the crop — a metaphor for the spiritually unsteady believer who is easily swayed by circumstances
key_terms.زَلَّتْ بِهِ قَدَمٌ: whose foot has slipped — a figurative expression for a believer who has faltered in upholding the full conditions of faith
key_terms.شُرُوطِهِ: His (Allah's) stipulations — the divine conditions and covenants incumbent upon a believer to fulfill
key_terms.يَشْفَعُ: intercedes — acts as an intercessor on behalf of others before Allah on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of believers (mu'minin) according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted through Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), classifies believers into two types: one who fully upholds the divine covenant with Allah, thereby earning a station alongside the Prophets, the Truthful, and the Martyrs as referenced in Quran 4:69, capable of interceding for others and immune from the terrors of both this world and the next; and one whose iman is unsteady — likened to a crop stalk swayed by wind — who faces tribulations in both worlds yet retains goodness and will ultimately be saved through shafa'ah. The hadith highlights that fulfillment of one's covenant with Allah is the decisive criterion separating the two ranks, while affirming that even the wavering believer is not abandoned by divine mercy.
